report.summary: Analyzed lint.py, checked all docstring and comment claims against the code.

handoff.purpose: Compute DOM-based metrics for UI surfaces, separating objective (Tier A) from proxy (Tier B) measurements.

symbols.name: BANNED_FACES
symbols.note: Tuple of typeface names considered generated defaults.

symbols.name: _looks_like_identifier
symbols.note: Heuristic to detect leaked internal names or raw JSON.

symbols.name: _lum
symbols.note: Compute relative luminance of an RGB color.

claims.text: Reads a capture from ``probe.js`` and computes metrics over the DOM/CSSOM.
claims.why: The chunk does not define or reference probe.js; it only reads a JSON file whose schema is assumed.

claims.text: No pixels are inspected; every number here is derived from geometry and computed style
claims.why: All metrics use element dimensions, position, computed style fields; no pixel-level analysis.

claims.text: Tier A metrics (contrast, overflow, target size, banned faces) measure things that are true or false. They can gate.
claims.why: The code defines Tier A metrics for horizontal_overflow, contrast_failures, small_targets, banned_faces, console_errors; all are objective counts.

claims.text: Tier B metrics are PROXIES for a judgement no rule can make.
claims.why: Tier B metrics (visible_elements, framed_panels, etc.) are computed and labelled tier B; no claim of objectivity.

claims.text: Every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it, so a disagreement is inspectable instead of arguable.
claims.why: Each Metric has an 'offenders' list containing evidence; to_dict includes offenders (truncated to 12).

claims.text: Thresholds are stamped ASSUMED until the corpus is large enough to earn MEASURED. Right now the corpus is n=4 (three rejected surfaces, one approved)
claims.why: No threshold values or corpus size tracking are present in this chunk.

claims.text: stdlib only, by design
claims.why: Imports are only from json, math, collections, dataclasses, pathlib; all stdlib.

claims.text: Faces that read as a generated default. Not a quality judgement about the typeface — a statement about what every AI dashboard already wears.
claims.why: BANNED_FACES includes inter, roboto, arial, space grotesk, geist, helvetica neue.

claims.text: Text that is a leaked internal name rather than something a person would say.
claims.why: _looks_like_identifier checks for JSON prefix, no spaces, underscores, alphanumeric, lowercase; matches the description.

claims.text: A framed surface, not a hairline divider or a text run.
claims.why: _is_panel requires borderSides >= 1, width >= 56, height >= 24; excludes thin dividers and small text runs.

claims.text: the page body must never scroll sideways
claims.why: horizontal_overflow metric uses scrollWidth - clientWidth; only positive values are flagged.

claims.text: WCAG AA: 4.5:1 body, 3.0:1 large
claims.why: Contrast threshold is 4.5 for normal text and 3.0 for large text (fontSize >=18 or bold >=14).

claims.text: interactive targets should reach 44x44
claims.why: small_targets metric flags elements with interactive flag and width <44 or height <44.

claims.text: grotesk defaults that mark a generated page
claims.why: banned_faces metric counts elements whose first font family is in BANNED_FACES.

claims.text: a broken page is not a design question
claims.why: console_errors metric counts entries from cap.get('consoleErrors', []).

claims.text: raw density of what is on screen at once
claims.why: visible_elements metric uses cap['elementsKept'] as value.

claims.text: when everything is a bordered box, nothing is elevated
claims.why: framed_panels metric counts panels (elements with border).

claims.text: more than two or three corner radii reads as unconsidered
claims.why: distinct_radii metric counts distinct rounded corner radius values among panels.

claims.text: frames inside frames inside frames
claims.why: panel_nesting_depth metric computes deepest chain of geometrically nested panels.

claims.text: shouted micro-labels used as decoration rather than hierarchy
claims.why: allcaps_text_share metric computes percentage of text in uppercase (via transform or isupper).

claims.text: if everything is flagged, nothing is flagged
claims.why: status_pills_visible metric counts small elements with pill shape (height <=32, radius >= height/2 -1.5, short text, border or background).

claims.text: an N-equal-tile metric row is the most recognisable trope in the category
claims.why: largest_equal_tile_row metric finds largest group of elements with similar width and height in same y-row.

claims.text: distinct 30-degree hue families in use, semantic colour included
claims.why: accent_hue_families metric counts hue buckets (30-degree bins) with at least 2 occurrences.

claims.text: internal field names and raw JSON rendered as user-facing text
claims.why: identifier_leaks metric uses _looks_like_identifier to detect leaked identifiers.

claims.text: Side-by-side table. The point of the whole exercise: do the numbers separate the surfaces a human rejected from the one he approved?
claims.why: compare function produces a table with human verdicts column if provided.

observations.what: Metric.to_dict truncates offenders to 12, but the docstring says 'every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it' without mentioning truncation; could be misleading.
The module claims 'stdlib only' but the CLI uses sys.argv and Path.read_text/write_text which are stdlib; no external dependencies.
The function main writes to 'runs/gui/report.json' but the docstring says 'usage: python -m daedalus.gui.lint runs/gui/*.json'; output path is hardcoded.
The claim about thresholds being ASSUMED vs MEASURED with n=4 is not backed by any code in this chunk; no threshold values or corpus size are present.
